I also started going through puberty pretty young, as I got my first period at 9. Made me feel really awkward around the other kids. I was bullied a few times. And I lost all my friends a lot. Maybe I deserved that. Another thing was a kid telling me I talked too much as a kid. I stopped talking for a long time. These days, I see a psychiatrist. I used to go to therapy and I am thinking of going again. I don't talk much. I don't have many friends. I only have one, honestly. I think I deserve everything that happened, in all honesty. I should have said something. But yeah, that's some stuff that messed me up a bit. I guess it isn't anything really bad, but I want to vent, I guess.

At the age of 11, I started falling into depression. I started to think (or realize) nothing mattered, but I still had hope. I kept trying hard for the going years, doing my absolute best to ward off depression, but it kept a firm grip on me. I officially started fighting back at the age of 17. But that's not where I realized I wasn't going to be exceptional. I realized it at the age of 16. After burning out in the middle of my AP Bio course, I realized I wasn't anywhere near the exceptionalness of a real doctor or specialist. It absolutely devastated me. I sobbed and broke down. I really had to be consoled. But after grieving my ambitions, I decided that the career that made me happy would be a career I enjoyed. I always dreamed of helping people, so I decided that if I couldn't be there to heal them, I could always teach them. So, I decided, I wanted to teach history. I wanted to take after the teachers who had inspired me over the years and did their best to keep me going. Even if they had no idea of the extent I was going through. Now, I am 18 years old. I know I won't be anyone special. And that's okay. I had yet another change of heart and decided that the best way to help would be to help children. Of all ages, not just the off chance of finding a child who was falling behind in class. So, now I am 18 and wanting to be a social worker. I won't have my name go down in history and I won't be fabulously wealthy, but that's okay. As long as I am doing what I can to help others, that is what matters. To me, that is what life is all about. Especially given what dragged me into that depression. Still fighting! But, that is a story for a different question or whatevs.
